text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#76431 — hosted-api > 99th latency spike + 500s across region-us-west. Triggered by prometheus/alerts/hosted_api_latency_high.
oncall-alex: acked. investigating. grabbing logs and flamegraphs.
oncall-alex: @taylor do you see anything on rollout side? we pushed canary ~ 2m ago.
taylor: on it, checking canary traces. nothing obvious in app traces but router metrics show a spike in request fanout to ephemeral backends.
amy (pd-bot): Escalation to L2 in 2m if not acknowledged. :rotating_light:
samir: also seeing transient 503s from the runtime pool; some workers cycling out with OOMKilled entries. possible mem pressure on dedicated nodes.
oncall-alex: capturing a snippet of the kube events: ```kubectl -n inference describe pod rtm-4f2c | tail -n 20\nEvents:\n  Warning  OOMKilled  2m  kubelet  Container crashed with out-of-memory````
jenna: i'm rebalancing a couple of heavy routes off of the suspected nodes, will reroute using routing-policy: prefer-healthy-az. doing a gradual drain on node rtm-4f2c.
oncall-alex: good call. toggling routing to prefer-healthy-az for hosted-api route. monitor dashboards for 30s.
PD-Bot: PagerDuty PD#76431 acknowledged by oncall-alex at 4391122336. No customer-facing incidents detected yet.
taylor: quick check: the canary model variant has kernel selection set to avx512 and quantized int8; mem footprint looks correct but the runtime shows an unusual KV-cache growth pattern. could be a KV-cache leak when certain long-prefix prompts hit.
samir: i pushed a short-lived hotfix: set KV_CACHE_LIMIT=200MB for production pool and restarted rtm-4f2c. rolling restart across two replicas.
oncall-alex: after KV cache limit and routing change, latency normalized at 4391122395. metrics: p99 from 1.2s -> 220ms.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD#76431 auto-resolved at 4391122410 (no further alerts).
taylor: noted a brief bump in error budget but no rate-limited customers. leaving canary paused until we root cause KV growth.
jenna: opening a follow-up ticket: INF-9821 "Investigate KV cache growth with long prefix prompts" with logs and heap snapshots attached. tagging samir and taylor.
oncall-alex: handoff to next oncall @taylor — please monitor next 15m for any reappearance, i'll write a short blameless note.
taylor: ack. i'll keep an eye on auto-resolve windows and watch PD for repeat.
jenna: quick customer check: alerted success-team slack and searched for external error reports — none found. pinged support to keep an ear out.
amy (pd-bot): PD#76431 closed. Summary: transient KV-cache growth + OOM on one runtime replica; mitigated by KV_CACHE_LIMIT and route preference change; auto-resolved.
oncall-alex: thanks team. postmortem assignment INF-9821 -> samir, taylor. will include hypothesis, reproducer, and mitigation plan (limit + autoscaler tuning).
jenna: adding a test with long-prefix synthetic prompts to the nightly eval to catch regressions.
taylor: logging follow-up checkpoints in the incident channel. final note: no customer impact. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
